findings.title: Access-token ID matcher rejects valid refresh tokens
findings.body: isAccessTokenId splits the jti on ':' and then treats items[0].substring(3, 5) as the grant shortcut, returning false when that slice equals the expected shortcut. The encoded prefix is six characters: session type [0,2), token type [2,4), grant type [4,6). substring(3, 5) is therefore the last character of the token type plus the first character of the grant, not the grant shortcut. For a normal refresh access token the prefix is like "onrtrt", so substring(3, 5) is "rt", the condition matches RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT, and the matcher returns false. expectRefresh() will fail every regular refresh-token event assertion. The same slice also does not actually check authorization-code, device, or CIBA shortcuts ("onrtac" yields "ta"), so those expectations pass even when the grant shortcut is wrong. Compare items[0].substring(4, 6) and fail when it does not equal the expected shortcut (and when the prefix length is not 6).

findings.title: Constructor null-check validates grantType twice, not rawTokenId
findings.body: The fourth requireNonNull call passes grantType again with the message "Null rawTokenId not allowed". A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and stored. encodeTokenId then concatenates it, producing a jti ending in ":null" (or an NPE later if a caller assumes the id is present). The check must be Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...).

findings.title: New getShortcut() breaks existing grant factories and is not length-checked
findings.body: getShortcut() was added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with no default implementation. Every existing custom grant factory fails to compile, and a deployed one throws AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit calls getShortcut(), which aborts server startup. The javadoc also says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId requires the whole context prefix to be exactly 6 characters (2+2+2) and throws IllegalArgumentException otherwise. Nothing in postInit or the hot-deploy refresh path checks that the shortcut is exactly two characters or that it does not collide with another grant after dynamic registration. A 3-character shortcut, which the new contract text encourages, is written into access-token jtis that can never be decoded.
